results.summary: The design covers the real-time fraud scoring path, novelty detection, behavioral features, graph-based ring analysis, adaptive retraining, explainability, and compliance reporting with a coherent low-latency serving and offline learning split.

findings.title: End-to-end fraud scoring and learning loop is well decomposed
findings.explanation: The architecture clearly separates request handling, authorization, feature retrieval, inference, audit, and asynchronous learning. This supports the core real-time path while keeping the training loop decoupled from the low-latency serving path.

findings.title: Explainability is carried through both decisioning and audit
findings.explanation: Reason codes are returned from scoring, versioned policy context is recorded, and the audit store retains lineage needed for compliance review.

results.summary: The architecture covers the full generative-media scope with coherent API, queue, GPU, serving, safety, storage, and delivery paths, including fine-tuning and short-video generation.

findings.title: Clear separation of interactive generation and offline fine-tuning
findings.explanation: The design cleanly splits request validation, generation execution, and custom-dataset fine-tuning into distinct orchestrator, worker, and GPU paths, which reduces coupling and makes the core workflows easier to evolve.

findings.title: Safety enforcement is integrated before public delivery
findings.explanation: Generated media is screened before release, unsafe or uncertain results are held for review, and only approved artifacts flow to the CDN and web workspace. This directly supports the safety requirement and reduces the risk of unsafe delivery.

findings.title: Queue and GPU design addresses concurrent demand and memory pressure
findings.explanation: The queue uses admission limits, fair dispatch, deadlines, and retry bounds while the GPU fleet adds memory-aware placement and autoscaling. This is a coherent response to the 10k+ concurrent-submission target and batch-memory constraint.

results.summary: The design covers the core clinical workflow, EHR integration, auditability, consent controls, and bounded image-analysis path well, but it does not explicitly close the published accuracy-validation constraint for supported conditions.

findings.title: No explicit clinical validation gate for the >95% accuracy target
findings.explanation: The architecture correctly limits inference to approved modalities and supported conditions, but it does not show how a model release is accepted only after meeting the published diagnostic accuracy threshold for those supported conditions. Without an explicit validation gate, the design can route to safe abstention, yet it still leaves the accuracy constraint unproven at the system level.
findings.recommendation: Add an approval gate in the model registry/release workflow that requires condition-level validation evidence, threshold checks, and versioned acceptance criteria before the serving path can use a model.

results.summary: The design covers the full perception scope with a coherent edge-hosted pipeline for multi-sensor fusion, 3D detection, tracking, and motion prediction.

findings.title: Well-structured perception pipeline from sensor ingestion to planning handoff
findings.explanation: The submission cleanly decomposes the perception stack into input, alignment, BEV fusion, tracking, and downstream motion handoff stages, which matches the published scope closely.

findings.title: Edge-hosted inference path aligns with latency and hardware constraints
findings.explanation: The design places inference on vehicle-local automotive-grade GPU hardware, which is the right architectural direction for the under-100ms and 30+ FPS constraints.

results.summary: The architecture provides a coherent, versioned legal-document analysis pipeline with secure ingestion, clause/risk extraction, semantic search, compliance review, summaries, and auditable results.

findings.title: End-to-end legal analysis pipeline is coherently grounded in evidence and versioning
findings.explanation: The design cleanly threads document version metadata, jurisdiction, ruleset, model version, and citations through ingestion, orchestration, storage, and audit recording. That directly supports contract review workflows without relying on opaque AI outputs.

findings.title: Access-controlled semantic retrieval is well integrated into the legal workflow
findings.explanation: The combination of ACL-prefiltered vector search, jurisdiction/version filters, and re-checks before passage return is a strong fit for sensitive repository search.

findings.title: Review-ready analysis is operationally observable
findings.explanation: Monitoring is scoped to the actual legal workflow: end-to-end latency, queue age, retries, OCR failures, model-serving errors, and quality measurement from reviewed labels.

results.summary: A cohesive AIOps incident-management design with clear paths for detection, correlation, impact analysis, routing, remediation suggestions, reporting, and learning, plus explicit safety gates and scale-oriented components.

findings.title: End-to-end incident workflow is well decomposed
findings.explanation: The submission separates monitoring, ingestion, correlation, impact analysis, routing, remediation, reporting, and learning into distinct services with clear responsibilities.

findings.title: Explicit safety gates reduce false merges and unsafe automation
findings.explanation: The design uses accuracy gating, conservative timeout fallback, human approval for runbooks, and authenticated policy checks, which are appropriate guardrails for AIOps incident handling.

results.summary: The design covers the core predictive auto-scaling flow well, including per-dimension forecasting, policy guardrails, dependency-aware execution, and outcome tracking, but it stops short of explicit controls for lead-time assurance and published constraint enforcement.

findings.title: Scale lead-time is not explicitly computed or enforced per service
findings.explanation: The design routes forecast lead-time context into policy and emits alerts, but it does not show a concrete mechanism that derives the required lead time from provider provisioning duration, workload warm-up time, or per-service deployment latency. Without that closed-loop timing calculation, the system can still approve actions that arrive too late for some services or dimensions.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit per-service lead-time estimator and a policy rule that blocks or accelerates actions when the estimated time-to-capacity exceeds the remaining demand window.

findings.title: Execution path does not show a bounded provisioning latency strategy
findings.explanation: The queue/worker/adapter chain is asynchronous and idempotent, which is good for throughput, but the architecture does not specify any pre-warming, deadline-aware prioritization, or latency budget for the scale operation itself. That leaves the actual scale-up completion time dependent on runtime conditions rather than a defined performance strategy.
findings.recommendation: Introduce an explicit execution-time budget, deadline prioritization, or pre-warm path for imminent spikes so the scaling workflow can meet the arrival window reliably.

findings.title: Cost reduction target is measured but not turned into an operational control
findings.explanation: Outcome analytics compare actual spend and over-provisioning to a baseline, but the design does not show a decision rule, optimization objective, or rollback trigger tied to the published 30% reduction goal. As written, it can observe cost savings without ensuring the architecture actively steers toward the target.
findings.recommendation: Add a cost-control loop that compares realized savings against the target and feeds the result into policy thresholds, model selection, or rollout gating.

findings.title: Published constraints are evaluated indirectly rather than explicitly closed
findings.explanation: The architecture has the right ingredients for accuracy, lead time, cost, and SLA monitoring, but it does not show an explicit end-to-end acceptance gate that proves the legacy constraints are met before promotion or fleet-wide rollout. In particular, the 15% forecast-accuracy target, zero late-scaling SLA misses, and 30% cost-reduction target are not shown as hard promotion criteria.
findings.recommendation: Define explicit rollout gates that check the published constraint set before promotion, and make constraint failures block deployment or trigger rollback.

results.summary: The design covers the RCA core scope with durable multi-signal ingestion, provenance-preserving correlation, graph-based dependency modeling, ranked causal hypotheses, and an operator feedback loop for continual improvement.

findings.title: Correlated evidence pipeline is well-structured
findings.explanation: The design cleanly separates ingestion, durable buffering, correlation, investigation, ranking, and review. That decomposition supports explainable RCA and makes the data flow easy to follow.

findings.title: Feedback loop supports continuous improvement
findings.explanation: Operator corrections are persisted with case evidence and fed into offline evaluation/training before model registry promotion, which is aligned with learning from reviewed incidents without destabilizing live ranking.

findings.title: Provenance is preserved across evidence and topology
findings.explanation: The design repeatedly retains source references, original timestamps, and graph provenance, which is important for operator trust and for distinguishing observed relationships from inferred propagation.

results.summary: The design covers ingestion, normalization, anomaly detection, unseen-pattern handling, correlation, trends, alerting, and hybrid natural-language search with coherent streaming, storage, and registry paths.

findings.title: Clear separation of hot-path analytics from cold-path training
findings.explanation: The design keeps online detection, trend aggregation, search indexing, and offline model evaluation in separate components, which reduces coupling and makes the log pipeline easier to evolve.

findings.title: Natural-language search is constrained rather than opaque
findings.explanation: The search path combines lexical retrieval, optional tenant-filtered vector similarity, and source-record verification under explicit authorization and time filters, which is a strong fit for log investigation.

findings.title: Template and model promotion is guarded by evaluation and rollback
findings.explanation: Versioned registry gates, format-stratified evaluation, and rollback-aware activation reduce the risk of promoting a parser or anomaly model that performs poorly on rare formats or critical patterns.

results.summary: The architecture covers the full alert-correlation scope with tenant-safe ingest, durable buffering, bounded dedup/correlation, fail-open critical routing, operator feedback loops, and monitoring for the stated targets.

findings.title: Tenant-scoped correlation and incident handling are well partitioned
findings.explanation: The design consistently carries tenant scope through ingest, normalization, correlation, storage, console access, and feedback learning, which reduces cross-tenant leakage risk and keeps incident state separable.

findings.title: Critical alerts have an explicit fail-open delivery path
findings.explanation: Critical actionable alerts bypass suppression policy and route directly to notification delivery, which is the right safety choice for the zero-suppression constraint.

findings.title: Offline learning is guarded before changing live policy
findings.explanation: Operator feedback is not applied directly; it is versioned, redacted, evaluated with safety gates, and only then canary-promoted, which limits the risk of bad labels affecting suppression behavior.
